title: Keyed Color Dungeon Map Reference — user screenshot example
subtitle: Map-key semantics reference

source.title: User-supplied keyed dungeon screenshots
source.notes: Reference added from user-supplied screenshots. The repository record captures the map-key interaction model and semantic legend. The original conversation screenshot bitmap is not falsely represented as a repository-backed source file.

general.purpose: Preserve a map style where colored or symbolic cells have meaningful legend entries that resolve to useful viewer information.

mapKey.label: Keyed location
mapKey.description: A numbered or named map location. Selecting the marker should open the associated room or area record rather than only identifying its color.

mapKey.label: Door / passage control
mapKey.description: An access point whose useful data includes what it connects, whether it is locked or secret, and any opening or break information.

mapKey.label: Stairs / level transition
mapKey.description: A transition between levels or elevations. The viewer should identify the destination deck or level when known.

mapKey.label: Trap / hazard
mapKey.description: A hazardous keyed cell. The detail view should expose trigger, detection, disable, consequence, and source notes when available.

mapKey.label: Encounter / creature
mapKey.description: A keyed encounter marker. The detail view should expose creatures, disposition, difficulty or level context, and encounter notes instead of a bare colored square.

mapKey.label: Treasure / reward
mapKey.description: A keyed reward or loot marker. The detail view should expose the actual treasure record, container or concealment details, and any access conditions.

mapKey.label: Special feature / point of interest
mapKey.description: A map-specific feature whose legend meaning must be preserved as text and linked to its descriptive or rules-facing record.
